title: Sexually Transmitted Infection Screening: Who to Test and Which Tests

evidenceAudit.scope: Adult or adolescent seen in primary care, antenatal, sexual health or emergency settings in Saudi Arabia who needs sexually transmitted infection (STI) screening: sexual history, who to test, which tests and specimens, pregnancy and premarital contexts, what to do with a positive result, treatment of chlamydia, gonorrhoea and syphilis, partner management and retesting. No open Saudi Ministry of Health STI screening guideline was found; the pathway follows the CDC 2021 STI Treatment Guidelines, with Saudi surveillance and primary-care studies for local context, and doses, dilution and administration from product labels.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 2026-10-20.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: No Saudi Ministry of Health STI screening guideline was opened. The Jeddah study refers to a Ministry of Health national syndromic management guideline that was not found online; clinicians should check it for local regimens and reporting rules.

Screening ages and groups follow CDC 2021 (United States) and the evidence base behind it; Saudi prevalence data are older (1995 to 1999 surveillance and a 2022 primary care survey) and do not support a Saudi-specific screening age.
Saudi premarital screening and reporting duties for notifiable infections were not verified from a primary source and are not written as rules here.

Doxycycline for syphilis in penicillin allergy, doxycycline post-exposure prophylaxis, human papillomavirus, herpes, trichomoniasis, hepatitis B and C treatment and HIV treatment are outside the regimens written here.
CDC 2021 may have been updated after publication; check the current CDC STI guidance for changes in regimens.
Doses, dilution, administration and contraindications come from the US labels named in each row; Saudi labels may differ.
Normal values for blood tests are standard reference values; laboratories differ.
Differentials follow standard clinical practice and were not drawn from one source section.
Figures were read through automated extraction of open-access journal XML and DailyMed label XML; spot-check each dose against the source during clinical review.
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register returned an empty page from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.

pathophysiology.summary: STIs spread through vaginal, anal or oral sex and from mother to baby; many infections cause no symptoms, so testing people who feel well finds disease that would otherwise spread or cause damage (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Clinical Prevention Guidance). Untreated chlamydia and gonorrhoea in women can ascend to cause pelvic inflammatory disease, ectopic pregnancy and infertility (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Chlamydial Infections and Gonococcal Infections). Syphilis passes through primary, secondary, latent and late stages; latent infection is found only by blood tests, and infection in pregnancy can infect the baby (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Syphilis). Having one STI raises the chance of having and passing on HIV, so testing for one prompts testing for the others (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, HIV Infection). In Saudi Arabia, the 1995 to 1999 national surveillance reported 39,049 STIs, mainly nongonococcal urethritis (37%), trichomoniasis (28%), gonococcal urethritis (14%), syphilis (9%) and HIV (7.5%); reporting is probably incomplete because of stigma (BMC Infect Dis 2006, Results). A 2022 survey of 47 Jeddah primary care physicians found that only about one third knew the Ministry of Health syndromic guideline and 6% had STI training, so many cases may be missed or poorly treated (Cureus 2022, Results).

symptoms: Often none; screening is for people with no symptoms (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Chlamydial Infections).
Urethral discharge or pain on passing urine (Cureus 2022, Results; CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Chlamydial Infections).
Vaginal discharge, lower abdominal pain, bleeding after sex (Cureus 2022, Introduction; CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Chlamydial Infections).
Genital sore, rash on palms or soles, or lumps in the groin (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Syphilis).
physicalSigns: Mucopurulent discharge, cervical friability or cervical motion tenderness (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Chlamydial Infections).
Painless ulcer (chancre) of primary syphilis; diffuse rash and mucous patches of secondary syphilis (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Syphilis).
Genital warts, painful vesicles or ulcers (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Genital Ulcers).
Epididymal tenderness or testicular swelling in a man with urethral symptoms (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Gonococcal Infections).
redFlags: Pregnancy with a positive STI test: treat immediately, notify the antenatal team and arrange test of cure; syphilis in pregnancy needs urgent penicillin and specialist review (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Pregnant Women).
Pelvic pain with fever, cervical motion tenderness or tubo-ovarian mass: pelvic inflammatory disease needs same-day treatment (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Chlamydial Infections).
Neurological, eye or ear symptoms with positive syphilis tests: neurosyphilis, ocular syphilis or otosyphilis needs urgent specialist assessment (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Syphilis).
Sexual assault or abuse of a child: follow the safeguarding and forensic pathway (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Sexual Assault and Abuse).
Positive HIV screening test: confirm and link to HIV care the same day; consider post-exposure prophylaxis if exposure was within 72 hours (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, HIV Infection).
precipitants: New sex partner, more than one partner or a partner with other partners (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Chlamydial Infections).
Previous or current STI (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Gonococcal Infections).
Age under 25 in women (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Chlamydial Infections).
Men who have sex with men; injecting drug use; sex in exchange for money or drugs (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Men Who Have Sex with Men).
Inconsistent condom use (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Gonococcal Infections).

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Frequency and burning with positive urine culture and no discharge; STI tests may still be needed in a sexually active person (clinical judgment).
Vaginal discharge with abnormal pH or yeast on microscopy and no cervicitis (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Vaginitis).

differentials.condition: Non-infectious genital ulcer (Behçet disease, trauma, fixed drug eruption)
differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Recurrent oral and genital ulcers or drug history with negative STI tests (clinical judgment).
Painful clustered vesicles or shallow ulcers; confirmed by herpes simplex virus nucleic acid test (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Genital Herpes).

differentials.condition: Epididymitis from a urinary tract pathogen
differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Older man, bladder outflow obstruction or urinary instrumentation (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Epididymitis).

differentials.condition: Pelvic inflammatory disease versus appendicitis or ectopic pregnancy
differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Check pregnancy test and ultrasound before diagnosing pelvic inflammatory disease (clinical judgment).

ruleIn.testName: Chlamydia and gonorrhoea nucleic acid amplification test (NAAT)
ruleIn.targetCondition: Chlamydia trachomatis and Neisseria gonorrhoeae infection
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Test at the site of exposure: vaginal swab or first-void urine in women (patient-collected swab is as good as clinician-collected), first-void urine in men, rectal or pharyngeal swab by exposure (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Chlamydial Infections, Diagnostic Considerations).

clinicalManagement.title: Take a sexual history and explain testing
actions: Ask about partners, practices, protection, past STIs and pregnancy intention in private and without judgment (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, STI and HIV Infection Risk Assessment).
Explain that testing is routine, confidential and voluntary; offer HIV testing opt-out (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, HIV Infection).
Ask about symptoms and examine if symptomatic (Cureus 2022, Introduction).

clinicalManagement.title: Decide who to test
actions: Test sexually active women under 25 and older women at higher risk for chlamydia and gonorrhoea every year (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Chlamydial Infections).
Test everyone aged 15 to 65 for HIV at least once, and everyone with an STI or new STI symptoms (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, HIV Infection).
Test all pregnant women at the first visit for HIV, syphilis and hepatitis B, and screen for hepatitis C (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Pregnant Women).
Test men who have sex with men at least yearly at each site of exposure (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Men Who Have Sex with Men).

clinicalManagement.title: Collect the right specimens
actions: Chlamydia and gonorrhoea: vaginal swab (can be self-collected) or first-void urine; rectal or pharyngeal swab by exposure (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Chlamydial Infections, Diagnostic Considerations).
Blood: HIV antigen/antibody, syphilis serology, hepatitis B and C as indicated (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Syphilis and Hepatitis sections).
Culture and susceptibility testing if gonorrhoea treatment failure is suspected (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Gonococcal Infections).

clinicalManagement.title: Act on a positive result
actions: Treat promptly and give the first dose in clinic (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Chlamydial Infections, Other Management Considerations).
Chlamydia: doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 7 days (azithromycin 1 g in pregnancy) (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Chlamydial Infection, Treatment).
Gonorrhoea: ceftriaxone 500 mg intramuscularly once, with doxycycline if chlamydia is not excluded (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Gonococcal Infection, Treatment).

Syphilis: benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units intramuscularly for primary, secondary and early latent disease; three weekly doses for late latent or unknown duration (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Syphilis, Treatment).
Test for the other STIs and HIV in anyone with a diagnosis (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Chlamydial Infection, Other Management Considerations).
Advise no sex for 7 days after treatment and until partners are treated (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Chlamydial Infection, Other Management Considerations).

clinicalManagement.title: Treat partners and follow the reporting rules
actions: Refer partners from the previous 60 days for testing and presumptive treatment (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Management of Sex Partners).

Check local legal rules on notification and expedited partner treatment before using them (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Reporting and Confidentiality; Saudi Ministry of Health notification rules not verified).
Protect confidentiality, especially for adolescents (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Adolescents).

clinicalManagement.title: Retest and follow up
actions: Retest all treated for chlamydia or gonorrhoea at 3 months (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Chlamydial Infections, Follow-Up).
Pregnancy with chlamydia: test of cure at 4 weeks (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Chlamydial Infection, Pregnancy).
Pharyngeal gonorrhoea: test of cure at 7 to 14 days (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Gonococcal Infection, Follow-Up).
Syphilis: clinical and blood review at 6, 12 and 24 months (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Syphilis, Follow-Up).
Offer hepatitis B vaccination and counselling on condoms and risk reduction (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Primary Prevention Methods).

regimens.indication: Uncomplicated urethral, cervical or rectal chlamydia in adults
regimens.dose: 100 mg twice daily for 7 days. Dilution and preparation: none; oral dose form, no reconstitution.
regimens.route: Oral, swallowed with a full glass of water to avoid oesophageal irritation; may be taken with food or milk if the stomach is upset (doxycycline label, Dosage and Administration)
regimens.duration: 7 days; abstain from sex until the course is finished and symptoms have gone (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Chlamydial Infection, Other Management Considerations)
adjustments: Pregnancy: avoid in the second and third trimesters because of tooth discoloration; use azithromycin (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Chlamydial Infection, Pregnancy).
Renal impairment: no excessive accumulation at usual doses (doxycycline label, Dosage and Administration).
Give the first dose in clinic and dispense all doses on-site (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Chlamydial Infection, Treatment).
Sunlight sensitivity, and separate from antacids, iron and calcium (doxycycline label, Precautions).
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register returned an empty page from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.
monitoring: Adherence and symptoms at 1 week by telephone or visit (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Chlamydial Infection, Follow-Up).
Retest at 3 months; test of cure only if adherence is doubtful, symptoms persist or she is pregnant (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Chlamydial Infection, Follow-Up).
Oesophagitis, photosensitivity rash, and diarrhoea (doxycycline label, Adverse Reactions).
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to any tetracycline (doxycycline label, Contraindications).
Pregnancy in the second or third trimester and children under 8 years, except in serious infection (doxycycline label, Warnings).
regimens.branch: Chlamydia found on screening or testing
regimens.useWhen: Preferred: more effective than azithromycin, especially for rectal infection.
regimens.sourceTitle: Doxycycline hyclate tablets: US prescribing information (DailyMed)
regimens.sourceEdition: CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Section Chlamydial Infections, Treatment; doxycycline hyclate US label, Dosage and Administration (Section Uncomplicated urethral, endocervical, or rectal infection)

regimens.indication: Uncomplicated chlamydia in pregnancy, or when adherence to a 7-day course is doubtful
regimens.patientGroup: Pregnant women and people unlikely to complete 7 days
regimens.dose: 1 g (two 500 mg tablets) as a single oral dose. Dilution and preparation: none; oral dose form, no reconstitution.
regimens.route: Oral, with or without food, as a single directly observed dose (azithromycin label, Dosage and Administration; CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Chlamydial Infection, Treatment)
regimens.duration: Single dose; abstain from sex for 7 days (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Chlamydial Infection, Other Management Considerations)
adjustments: Pregnancy: safe and effective; recommended regimen; test of cure at 4 weeks and retest at 3 months (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Chlamydial Infection, Pregnancy).
Hepatic: avoid in a history of cholestatic jaundice with azithromycin (azithromycin label, Section 4.2).
Caution with QT prolongation, torsades de pointes history, bradyarrhythmia, heart failure or QT-prolonging drugs (azithromycin label, Section 5.4).
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register returned an empty page from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.
monitoring: Nausea, diarrhoea and abdominal pain are common after the single dose (azithromycin label, Adverse Reactions).
Test of cure at 4 weeks in pregnancy; retest at 3 months for all (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Chlamydial Infection, Follow-Up).
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to azithromycin, erythromycin, any macrolide or ketolide (azithromycin label, Section 4.1).
History of cholestatic jaundice or hepatic dysfunction with prior azithromycin (azithromycin label, Section 4.2).
regimens.branch: Chlamydia found on screening or testing
regimens.useWhen: Choose in pregnancy, or when a single directly observed dose is needed for adherence; less effective than doxycycline for rectal infection.
regimens.sourceEdition: CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Section Chlamydial Infections, Treatment and Pregnancy; Zithromax US label, Section 2.1, Section 4 and Section 5.4

regimens.indication: Uncomplicated gonorrhoea of the cervix, urethra, rectum or pharynx
regimens.patientGroup: Adults and adolescents under 150 kg, including pregnant women
regimens.dose: 500 mg as a single intramuscular dose (1 g if weight 150 kg or more). Dilution and preparation: for a 500 mg vial add 1.8 mL of diluent to make about 250 mg/mL (or 1 mL for 350 mg/mL); shake until dissolved and withdraw the whole contents; the label lists sterile water for injection, 0.9% sodium chloride, 5% dextrose, bacteriostatic water, or 1% lidocaine (without epinephrine) as diluents; the 1 g dose needs 3.6 mL of diluent at 250 mg/mL (2 vials of 500 mg or one 1 g vial). Never give a lidocaine solution intravenously.
regimens.route: Deep intramuscular injection well within a large muscle (gluteal); aspirate first to avoid a blood vessel (ceftriaxone label, Intramuscular Administration)
regimens.duration: Single dose; abstain from sex for 7 days and until partners are treated
adjustments: Add doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 7 days if chlamydia has not been excluded (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Gonococcal Infection, Treatment).
Pregnancy: same regimen (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Gonococcal Infection, Pregnancy).
No dose change for renal or hepatic impairment (ceftriaxone label, Dosage and Administration).

Penicillin allergy: cross-reactivity with third-generation cephalosporins is under 1%; if IgE-mediated allergy is strongly suspected, use gentamicin 240 mg IM plus azithromycin 2 g orally and consult a specialist (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Gonococcal Infection, Drug Allergy).
Do not mix with calcium-containing intravenous solutions (ceftriaxone label, Compatibility and Stability).
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register returned an empty page from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.
monitoring: Return if symptoms persist 3 to 5 days after treatment: culture and susceptibility testing (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Gonococcal Infection, Suspected Cephalosporin Treatment Failure).
Pharyngeal gonorrhoea: test of cure at 7 to 14 days (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Gonococcal Infection, Follow-Up).
Retest at 3 months; test for HIV, syphilis and chlamydia (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Gonococcal Infection, Other Management Considerations).
Observe for 15 to 30 minutes for hypersensitivity (ceftriaxone label, Warnings).
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to ceftriaxone, its excipients or any cephalosporin (ceftriaxone label, Contraindications).
Premature or hyperbilirubinaemic neonates, and neonates needing calcium-containing intravenous solutions (ceftriaxone label, Contraindications).
If lidocaine is the diluent: contraindications to lidocaine apply (ceftriaxone label, Contraindications, Lidocaine).
regimens.branch: Gonorrhoea found on screening or testing
regimens.sourceTitle: Ceftriaxone for injection USP: US prescribing information (DailyMed)
regimens.sourceEdition: CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Section Gonococcal Infections, Treatment; ceftriaxone for injection US label, Section Directions for Use: Intramuscular Administration and Section Contraindications

regimens.indication: Primary, secondary and early latent syphilis (single dose); late latent or unknown duration (three doses)
regimens.patientGroup: Non-pregnant adults and adolescents without neurological, eye or ear involvement and without penicillin allergy
regimens.dose: 2.4 million units as a single intramuscular dose for primary, secondary and early latent syphilis; for late latent syphilis or unknown duration give 2.4 million units once a week for 3 weeks (7.2 million units total). Dilution and preparation: ready-to-use suspension in prefilled syringes (4 mL syringe holds 2.4 million units; 2 mL holds 1.2 million units); do not dilute or mix; keep refrigerated at 2 to 8 degrees Celsius and do not freeze; a 2.4 million unit dose can be given as one 4 mL injection or as two 1.2 million unit injections at separate sites. Other penicillin formulations (procaine, crystalline) are not interchangeable (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Syphilis, Treatment).
regimens.route: Deep intramuscular injection only, slowly and steadily, into the upper outer buttock or ventrogluteal site; never intravenous, intra-arterial or near a nerve (Bicillin L-A label, Method of Administration)
regimens.frequency: Single dose, or weekly for 3 weeks
regimens.duration: 1 dose or 3 doses; for late latent disease a gap of 10 to 14 days between doses may be acceptable in non-pregnant persons (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Syphilis, Latent Syphilis)
adjustments: Pregnancy: parenteral penicillin G is the only therapy with documented efficacy; a pregnant woman with penicillin allergy must be desensitised and treated with penicillin (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Syphilis, Pregnancy).

Penicillin allergy outside pregnancy: doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 2 weeks (early) or 4 weeks (late) may be used if follow-up is assured (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Syphilis, Penicillin Allergy; doxycycline label).
Infants and children: 50,000 units/kg to a maximum of 2.4 million units (Bicillin L-A label, Dosage and Administration).
Warn about the Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction (fever and malaise within 24 hours) (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Syphilis, Jarisch-Herxheimer Reaction).
Not for neurosyphilis, ocular or otic syphilis, which need aqueous penicillin G intravenously under a specialist (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Neurosyphilis).
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register returned an empty page from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.
monitoring: Clinical and non-treponemal titre review at 6 and 12 months (and 24 months for latent disease) (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Syphilis, Follow-Up).
Test for HIV and other STIs at diagnosis (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Syphilis, Other Management Considerations).
Anaphylaxis, injection-site reactions and neurovascular injury (Bicillin L-A label, Warnings).
Treat sexual contacts within 90 days presumptively (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Syphilis, Management of Sex Partners).
contraindications: History of a hypersensitivity reaction to any penicillin (Bicillin L-A label, Contraindications).
Not for intravenous use: cardiorespiratory arrest and death have followed inadvertent intravenous injection (Bicillin L-A label, Warning).

branches.label: Chlamydia found on screening or testing
branches.entryCriteria: Positive chlamydia nucleic acid amplification test (urogenital, rectal or pharyngeal), with no features of pelvic inflammatory disease, epididymitis or complicated infection, and no allergy to the chosen drug.

branches.label: Gonorrhoea found on screening or testing
branches.entryCriteria: Positive gonorrhoea test or clinical urethritis or cervicitis with intracellular diplococci, with no features of disseminated or complicated infection; not allergic to cephalosporins.

branches.label: Syphilis found on screening or testing
branches.entryCriteria: Reactive treponemal and non-treponemal syphilis tests with primary, secondary or latent disease, no neurological, ocular or ear symptoms and no penicillin allergy.

medicationPlan.note: Regimens follow CDC STI Treatment Guidelines 2021; doses, dilution, administration and contraindications come from the US product labels named in each row. All doses are for non-pregnant adults unless stated. Treatment for HIV, hepatitis, herpes and trichomoniasis is not written here. diagnosticCriteria.criterion: Women under 25 who are sexually active: chlamydia and gonorrhoea
diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Screen every year (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Chlamydial Infections and Gonococcal Infections).

diagnosticCriteria.criterion: Women 25 or older at higher risk
diagnosticCriteria.threshold: New partner, more than one partner, partner with concurrent partners or partner with an STI: screen for chlamydia and gonorrhoea every year (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Chlamydial Infections).
Test everyone aged 15 to 65 at least once, everyone seeking STI evaluation, and higher-risk persons every year; use opt-out testing (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, HIV Infection).

At the first visit test for HIV, syphilis and hepatitis B surface antigen; screen for chlamydia and gonorrhoea if under 25 or at increased risk; screen for hepatitis C each pregnancy; retest in the third trimester if at risk (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Pregnant Women).

diagnosticCriteria.criterion: Men who have sex with men
diagnosticCriteria.threshold: At least yearly HIV, syphilis, and chlamydia and gonorrhoea at each site of exposure (urine, rectal, pharyngeal); every 3 to 6 months if high risk (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Men Who Have Sex with Men).
Screen all adults aged 18 or older at least once, except where prevalence is under 0.1% (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Hepatitis C Virus).

Screening asymptomatic men who have sex only with women for chlamydia or gonorrhoea; routine screening for trichomoniasis, bacterial vaginosis or herpes in the general population (CDC STI Guidelines 2021, Adolescents).

guidelineComparison.note: The CDC pathway is applied because no open Saudi screening guideline was found; local rules must be checked.

teaching.scope: Adult or adolescent seen in primary care, antenatal, sexual health or emergency settings in Saudi Arabia who needs sexually transmitted infection (STI) screening: sexual history, who to test, which tests and specimens, pregnancy and premarital contexts, what to do with a positive result, treatment of chlamydia, gonorrhoea and syphilis, partner management and retesting. No open Saudi Ministry of Health STI screening guideline was found; the pathway follows the CDC 2021 STI Treatment Guidelines, with Saudi surveillance and primary-care studies for local context, and doses, dilution and administration from product labels.
learningObjectives: Ask a private sexual history and offer testing to everyone at risk.
Screen women under 25 yearly for chlamydia and gonorrhoea; test everyone for HIV once.
Test pregnant women at the first visit for HIV, syphilis and hepatitis B.
Treat on the day, treat partners, and retest at 3 months.
pitfalls: Testing only the urine in someone with rectal or throat exposure.
Giving the wrong penicillin formulation for syphilis.
keyPoints: Chlamydia and gonorrhoea tests must come from the site of exposure.
Ceftriaxone 500 mg intramuscularly for gonorrhoea; add doxycycline unless chlamydia is excluded.
Benzathine penicillin is deep intramuscular only and never intravenous.
A positive STI test calls for HIV and syphilis testing.

patientEducation: Many infections have no symptoms, so testing is advised even if you feel well.
Take all your tablets; do not have sex until 7 days after treatment and until your partner is treated.
Condoms lower the risk of infection.
Come back for a repeat test in 3 months.
lifestyleAndDiet: Limit the number of partners and avoid overlapping partners.
Get hepatitis B vaccine if you are not immune.
Have regular tests if your risk continues.
mdtReferrals: Primary care physician; nurse or sexual health nurse; obstetrician for pregnancy; infectious diseases physician; microbiologist; public health team for notification and partner services; counsellor or social worker; pharmacist.
dischargeCriteria: Specimens taken, first dose given, partner plan agreed, advice on abstaining and condoms given, results follow-up arranged, and a retest booked for 3 months.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Chlamydia and gonorrhoea: retest at 3 months; test of cure at 4 weeks for chlamydia in pregnancy and at 7 to 14 days for pharyngeal gonorrhoea. Syphilis: clinical review and non-treponemal titre at 6, 12 and 24 months. Repeat HIV and other screening yearly while risk continues.
